hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic to Florida roads
hero.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home this Fourth of July weekend, marking an all-time high for the holiday.
hero.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with AAA estimating 72.2 million people will have journeyed at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that total, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day.

Friday's wet weather created difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd said the conditions were "really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the challenging weather, drivers continued their holiday trips. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of a shrinking spending plan. The term-limited Governor exercised his line-item veto authority to cut nearly $810 million from the budget, along with blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or maybe nice to have, though he noted he was not trying to set a record. In 2022, DeSantis vetoed a record-breaking $3.1 billion in state budget funds. The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The spending plan also sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades.

Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers salaries. The Legislature had included the $750 million rainy-day fund transfer to prepare for a proposed constitutional amendment passed by the House last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to shoot down 621 projects or budget turkeys worth $830 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year budget.

DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations from the budget that Florida TaxWatch wanted slashed. The Governor also indicated he does not plan to be formally involved with any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals, though he left open the possibility of responding to individual requests for support. The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his final term as Governor.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit stations two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County maritime teams are deploying two boats with medics in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters celebrate the Fourth of July weekend on the water.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team expects hundreds of boaters on the water this Fourth of July weekend. The unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of Martin County.

Harry said the medics will assist with injuries ranging from stubbed toes to cardiac issues and potential spinal injuries. Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched their boat Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy, saying safety is their top priority.

Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. He encouraged boaters to have fun and be safe during the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating as Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County earned an A rating from the state for the third consecutive year, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B and a record 93.5% graduation rate.
cards.body:
S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach Jumps From C to A Rating as Palm Beach County Schools Earn Third Consecutive A

The School District of Palm Beach County has earned an A rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, marking continued academic excellence across the district. This year, 143 district-operated schools received either an A or B rating, an increase from 120 schools the previous year. The district also achieved a record graduation rate of 93.5%. School grades in Florida are determined by multiple factors, including student performance on state tests, graduation rates, and performance in advanced coursework. Additionally, 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. A total of 144 recent graduates earned associate degrees alongside their high school diplomas.

One of the most notable success stories involves S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which made a remarkable leap from a C rating to an A rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has led the school as principal for 15 years and previously served as assistant principal for five years, attributed the improvement to strategic changes implemented three years ago. The school modified its early childhood curriculum program, which serves students starting at age 3 and integrates with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and demonstrating higher academic performance levels. Tata explained that the school also refined its overall academic approach, focusing on challenging both students and staff to raise expectations across the campus. She noted the school had previously earned an A rating two years ago and narrowly missed achieving a B rating last year by just a few points.

Three other district schools also improved from C to A ratings this year: Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary. Superintendent Mike Burke praised the district's accomplishments, stating that the A rating "reflects our ongoing commitment to sparking academic success and helping every student ignite their future."

Community member Chris Ceasar, who attended Spady as a child and has family members currently enrolled there, expressed enthusiasm about the school's transformation. "For them to be an A school from a C school, that's a huge jump," Ceasar said. "It's a big thing for the community because education is first in Delray Beach." He added that the improved rating would attract more talent to the school. Tata emphasized the collaborative effort behind the achievement, saying "There is a lot of work that went on behind the scenes" and that students and staff "brought everything to the table and did everything that they were supposed to do."

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city honored this year.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach received the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, becoming the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. One of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the award, Riviera Beach was recognized during the National Civic League conference in Denver. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, noting that "little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program providing mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that the award is a tribute to community heart and determination. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors. City leaders said the designation positions the community for future opportunities and reinforces that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration drives results.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009. Theobald was suspended last year following Facebook comments labeling conservative activist Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In its filing, the school board's attorney argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone's findings "are not based upon competent substantial evidence" and characterized Theobald's Facebook post as a "serious offense" that warranted removal.

Livingstone issued her recommendation last month, citing a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that found disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Theobald told WPTV the case raises questions about where boundaries should be drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. The school board retains final decision-making authority on whether to reinstate Theobald, with no timeline announced for a ruling.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County deputies crack down on impaired driving
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County deputies are conducting enforcement operations targeting impaired drivers.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office deputies are stepping up enforcement against impaired driving. The crackdown comes during the Fourth of July holiday weekend.

Deputies are conducting patrols and checkpoints to identify and arrest drivers operating vehicles under the influence of alcohol or drugs. The operation aims to reduce traffic crashes and keep roads safer during the holiday period.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents demand fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as trespassing disputes escalate
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach say people using the JB-7 public beach walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed a fence in 2023, leading to confrontations and police calls.
cards.body:
A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach access point in Juno Beach has created tension between Colony Condos residents and summer beachgoers. The town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons, leaving only bushes to separate the public access path from private property. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer when cars park randomly and people push back bushes with their coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs to cut through private land. Hill said residents used to confront trespassers and tell them it was private property, but people would get rude, so now they call the police instead.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, suggesting the town could help with a lower-cost fence or a combination of split rail and shrubs. Hill said residents hope the town will reinstall the fence so they can have their landscaping and private parking back. The council agreed to address the fence question during its budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby as hundreds of boaters expected for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters celebrate the Fourth of July weekend on local waterways.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit Martin County waterways this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with the Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team will have two boats with medics on standby positioned in the north and south parts of the county to respond to emergencies. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, are taking extra precautions on the water. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water. Harry urged boaters to do their part by keeping their eyes on the water, having a designated driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community launches fundraiser for man who lost fiancee in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed the couple's belongings.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, described the scene as "completely a state of devastation." Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, playing the piano, kids and people, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his one and only child, Jacob, in a previous tragedy. White's birthday was July 4, just a few days after she passed away. Fenn said White will always be in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied reconstruction coverage by Anthem hours before surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage for her breast reconstruction surgery by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before the procedure, which involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health."

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that has become a controversial treatment for breast reconstruction. While it is popular among plastic surgeons and approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and is still considered an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined." Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago thanks to her plastic surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, who worked tirelessly to find a mechanism to make it happen. An Anthem spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards, and that without FDA approval, the mesh does not currently meet the standards required for coverage. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% as ground beef and strawberry prices rise
hero.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
Americans planning Fourth of July cookouts this year will need to dig deeper into their wallets. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase from last year. The price hike reflects broader economic pressures affecting groceries across the board, with some items seeing significantly steeper increases than others.

Inflation is the primary driver behind the rising cookout costs. Ground beef prices have climbed 5.5% compared to a year ago, while hamburger buns have become 7.7% more expensive. Strawberries have experienced the most dramatic price jump at 12.4%, a spike largely attributed to frost damage in Florida's growing regions. Ice cream, another cookout staple, is up 5.3%. These increases compound to make traditional summer meals noticeably pricier for households across the country.

However, not all cookout ingredients are following the upward price trend. Potato prices have actually declined this year, offering relief to consumers who enjoy potato chips and potato salad at their gatherings. Corn prices have been more volatile, though shoppers can find good deals on locally grown corn from the Glades region. These price decreases provide some opportunity for families to offset costs in other areas of their menus.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies to manage Fourth of July expenses. The first step is to compare prices across different grocery stores to identify which retailers offer the best deals on items on your shopping list. Woroch emphasizes that the most impactful way families can control costs is by reducing food waste, which starts with creating a detailed meal plan before shopping. By planning meals in advance, households can purchase only what they need and avoid the common problem of throwing away unused groceries. These practical approaches can help families enjoy their Independence Day celebrations without breaking the budget.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike on Midway Road.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is currently a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike in Port St. Lucie. According to Samples, the interchange is about accessibility and accommodating growth in the city over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which remains in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. The city council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach considers elevated autonomous transit connecting downtown to airport
cards.teaser: California-based Glydways will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. The company estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin deeper discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing, with a planning and design contract potentially awarded later this year.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Peacock House Art Foundation attracts global artists to historic Crain Estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain while connecting local and international artists through an artist-in-residency program.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates from the historic Crain Estate, where Jaxson Crain, a tile worker by trade, crafted all the tiling throughout the facility from ground to walls to ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Many parts of the house remain unchanged from when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and prestained glass leading to the front patio bar. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. Art director Krystal Masters said the estate is 90 percent the way it was when the Crains were present.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven that have since grown to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable because he walks with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world and offers simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab provides classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including one-on-one instruction in sculpting and watercolor designed for complete beginners. Masters said art is a form of therapy that destresses people.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire as community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a fire at her Hobe Sound home on Monday. The sheriff's office is investigating the blaze, with preliminary findings pointing to an electrical issue as a possible cause. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, who knew White for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. She said White was always the first to lend a hand and loved kids and people. The loss carries added grief for Mark, who previously lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday was the Fourth of July, meaning she passed just days before turning another year older. Fenn said White's memory will always be in their hearts.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closing Monday for $3 million renovation to expand slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long $3 million renovation that will nearly double its capacity from 18 to 44 slips for both motorize.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long, $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. Funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, the renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, said the dock has needed work and expressed hope for more floating docks. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, initially faced concerns about continuing operations during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for the company, said the city found a solution by allowing the business to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the dock for passenger boarding. Kuyrkendall said the dock plays a central role in the city's identity and economy, particularly on weekends when space becomes limited.

hero.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
hero.teaser: The Martin County School Board is challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended after making social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
hero.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended following Facebook comments labeling Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone recommended Theobald be reinstated with back pay and benefits. In her order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights.

The Martin County School Board is challenging the judge's recommendation. In a Thursday court filing, the board's attorney argued that Livingstone's findings "are not based upon competent substantial evidence" and called Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk a "serious offense," saying his removal was appropriate. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority to decide whether Theobald returns to his position, with no timeline announced for that determination.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit stations two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County maritime teams are deploying two boats with medics in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters celebrate the Fourth of July weekend on the water.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team expects hundreds of boaters on the water this Fourth of July weekend. The unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of Martin County.

Harry said the medics will assist with injuries ranging from stubbed toes to cardiac issues and potential spinal injuries. Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched their boat Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy, saying safety is their top priority.

Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. He encouraged boaters to have fun and be safe during the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation adding 26 boat slips
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long $3 million renovation that will expand capacity from 18 to 44 slips for motorized and non-motorized vessels.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees and will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing his company to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the dock so passengers can continue boarding during construction. Kuyrkendall said modernizing and expanding the dock will benefit both the city and businesses that operate there.

cards.headline: Heavy traffic and rain hit South Florida roads as record Fourth of July travel continues
cards.teaser: Record Fourth of July travel numbers are bringing heavy traffic to South Florida roads, with AAA estimating 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home during the holiday period.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with South Florida drivers navigating heavy rain and crowded roads. AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, with 61.4 million making the trip by car. Friday's wet weather created challenging conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd described the impact of the rain, saying "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the difficult conditions, some drivers managed smoother experiences. Carlos Borras and his wife completed their round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday without incident, with Borras reporting "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great."

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. However, driver Fernando Amado experienced heavier congestion, noting "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather." For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends departing after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid peak congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of only 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change.

Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Riviera Beach's application highlighted the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program providing mini-grants to longtime homeowners for critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of the community and reinforces the city's positive momentum. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient and surgeon speak out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, a 48-year-old breast cancer patient, and her surgeon are speaking out after Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy and planned reconstruction surgery using GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh. However, less than 24 hours before the procedure, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage, stating the surgery is "investigational" and lacks sufficient proof it improves health. According to a 2023 FDA letter, the efficacy and safety of GalaFlex for breast cancer patients have not been determined. While the mesh is FDA-approved for some uses in the body and popular among plastic surgeons, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains considered off-label and experimental.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and argues it produces fewer complications than other options. Billington has publicly criticized insurance denials on social media, joining doctors calling for policy changes. Clark underwent the reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to proceed. Last year, after investigative reporting by Katie LaGrone and Matthew Apthorp, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Clark and Billington continue fighting Anthem's denial. A new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health & Cancer Rights Act.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is targeting a state title in the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. However, a second-round playoff exit has motivated the program to push for deeper postseason success. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson emphasized the strength of his senior class, noting that most are four-year players who came through the middle school program. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To advance further in the playoffs, the Scots have intentionally scheduled tougher opponents for the upcoming season. Senior Jack Williams explained the strategy: "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people." Senior Jack Whelche stressed that playoff advancement, not regular season records, defines success: "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs."

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering a variety of educational programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Independence Day with fireworks and pool party at country club
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida offers free state park admission for America's 250th Independence Day
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is waiving admission fees at state parks from Friday through Sunday to celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection announced that all residents and visitors can explore state parks for free from July 3 through July 5, 2026, to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends and their family to the state parks to enjoy the outdoors, make new memories and support treasured public lands. The free admission offer applies to day use only, with all other fees, including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals, remaining in effect.

The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award, showcasing state investment in protecting natural resources while maintaining public access and environmental stewardship. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks saw more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated $3.6 billion in statewide economic impact. Parks offer hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding, along with historic sites including forts, battlefields, archaeological sites and other historic landmarks. Three parks are excluded from the free admission offer: Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park. Visitors can find the nearest park at FloridaStateParks.org.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of a shrinking spending plan. The term-limited Governor exercised his line-item veto authority to cut nearly $810 million from the budget, along with blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or maybe nice to have, though he noted he was not trying to set a record. In 2022, DeSantis vetoed a record-breaking $3.1 billion in state budget funds. The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The spending plan also sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades.

Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers salaries. The Legislature had included the $750 million rainy-day fund transfer to prepare for a proposed constitutional amendment passed by the House last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to shoot down 621 projects or budget turkeys worth $830 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year budget.

DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations from the budget that Florida TaxWatch wanted slashed. The Governor also indicated he does not plan to be formally involved with any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals, though he left open the possibility of responding to individual requests for support. The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his final term as Governor.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities host fireworks and parades for America's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Cities from Sarasota to Fort Myers Beach are staging waterfront celebrations, drone shows and patriotic parades to mark the semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Fourth of July weekend is bringing fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations across Southwest Florida as communities mark America's 250th birthday. The semiquincentennial gives this year's Independence Day events a special anniversary hook, with festivities planned from Sarasota's bayfront and Nathan Benderson Park to Manatee County, Venice, North Port and Fort Myers Beach.

Bradenton and Palmetto will celebrate together with festivities on both sides of the Manatee River, including activities along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest at Riverside Park will feature 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a "Lil Firecrackers" kids zone and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the Manatee River. Sarasota's bayfront will host an America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m., while Siesta Beach will present its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., 100% funded by local residents, businesses and community supporters. Venice will celebrate both America250 and the city's centennial with a patriotic parade through Historic Downtown Venice beginning at 9:30 a.m. at West Venice Avenue and Avenue des Parques, with the America250 fireworks show scheduled to start between 9 to 9:15 p.m. at the South Jetty. Fort Myers Beach will kick off celebrations with a parade at 10 a.m. starting at Bay Oaks Recreation Center and heading down Estero Boulevard to Times Square, followed by fireworks launched from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m., with Matanzas Pass Bridge closing from around 8:30 to 11:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Delray Beach opens 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule for America's 250th celebration
cards.teaser: The city will open a half-century old time capsule at its Fourth of July celebration, one of dozens of Florida events on the national America250 calendar.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition for more than 50 years that draws upward of 20,000 people to the Village by the Sea, is an official America250 partner event marking the nation's 250th anniversary. The city will open a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule on the Main Stage at A1A, a half-century message from Americans who celebrated the nation's 200th birthday to those marking its 250th. At 6 p.m., a 60-foot flag rises at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue alongside the National Anthem and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society.

The beach day begins at 8 a.m. with the 4's on the 4th volleyball tournament and the Star Spangled Sandcastles contest, the city's sand-sculpting showdown presented by local Rotary and Kiwanis clubs. Judging takes place at 11 a.m., with a house rule to keep creations patriotic, not political. From noon to 1 p.m., guided snorkel and scuba tours explore the S.S. Inchulva, the British steamship that a 1903 hurricane tore apart 150 yards offshore. Evening brings tribute act Let's Groove Tonight channeling Earth, Wind & Fire and DJ SoNyce on the Main Stage, with Digital Vibez on the East Road Stage from 6:30 to 9 p.m. A Zambelli fireworks display lights up the Atlantic at 9 p.m. Roads close from noon to 11 p.m., and the city urges visitors to park west of the Intracoastal Bridge with free FreeBee rides circulating downtown.

cards.headline: Marion County stages four synchronized fireworks displays for semiquincentennial
cards.teaser: Ocala and Marion County are hosting fireworks at four sites, parades and free aquatic center access as part of Marion Celebrates 250.
cards.body:
Marion County will stage synchronized fireworks displays at four sites on July 4 to commemorate America250, the semiquincentennial marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Each display steps off at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors and family activities before fireworks light up the sky at 9 p.m. The locations are Veterans Memorial Park in Ocala, Wrigley Fields in Citra, Dunnellon High School in Dunnellon and the Belleview Sportsplex in Belleview.

The city of Ocala hosts Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park starting at 10 a.m., a free celebration featuring live music, food trucks, a kids zone and games. Country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette performs from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is also opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads and the Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties and activities the same day. The Patriot Parade kicks off at Southeast 16th Avenue, heads up Silver Springs Boulevard and concludes near Southeast 25th Avenue, with veteran groups, local businesses and community organizations marching in the early evening. Marion County is promoting the "Explore Your Freedom Here" theme all summer, highlighting crystal-clear springs, trails, the World Equestrian Center and locally owned restaurants and breweries.

cards.headline: Voting rights activist warns of rollback attempts on America's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Michael Waldman ties the semiquincentennial to the ongoing struggle to fulfill the Declaration of Independence's promise of expanded voting rights.
cards.body:
Michael Waldman argues that the country's 250th anniversary celebration must remind Americans that the nation's story is a long struggle to fulfill the promise of the Declaration of Independence, and that the issues consuming the country today were central to the changes brought by the Revolution. From the start, the right to vote required a fight to vote. In 1776, only white men who owned property had the franchise, a legacy from the British. Pennsylvania's radical new charter gave the right to vote to all men, even those without property, and historians believe to many Black men, with Benjamin Franklin as the principal author.

Waldman notes that the property requirement ended during Andrew Jackson's presidency, when angry white working-class men won the first voting rights victory. Black men won the right to vote in part by serving in the U.S. Army in massive numbers, with one in five Union soldiers being Black by the end of the Civil War. Women won the vote through the 19th Amendment, having pioneered protest tactics such as peaceful marches and hunger strikes. The Voting Rights Act of 1965 created a multiracial democracy in the United States for the first time. Waldman warns that people in power are yet again trying to roll back the right to vote.

cards.headline: More than 100 new Florida laws take effect July 1
cards.teaser: A wave of legislation ranging from administrative to obscure went into effect at the start of the month, with some potentially affecting daily life.
cards.body:
More than 100 bills took effect in Florida on July 1, ranging from administrative to obscure provisions. Some of the new laws could affect daily life for residents across the state, though specific details about individual measures were not provided in available reporting.

The legislation covers areas including schools and other aspects of Florida governance. The broad scope of the new laws reflects the scale of the legislative session and the variety of policy areas addressed by state lawmakers during the session that concluded earlier this year.

hero.teaser: Firefighters responded to a structure fire at an abandoned building in Jensen Beach.
hero.body:
Multiple agencies extinguished a fire at an abandoned structure in Jensen Beach on Saturday. Firefighters responded to the blaze and brought it under control.

The fire occurred at a vacant building in the Jensen Beach area. Agencies worked together to extinguish the flames at the abandoned structure.

Salty Pelican Fish Shack in Hobe Sound was the subject of a Florida restaurant review. The Hobe Sound establishment was profiled as part of coverage of Florida dining options.

Communities in the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast are celebrating America's 250th anniversary on this Fourth of July. The milestone marks 250 years since the Declaration of Independence.

Local communities across the Treasure Coast are holding events to commemorate the historic anniversary. The celebrations are taking place throughout the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast region.

Businesses and government offices across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast adjusted operations for the July Fourth holiday. The closures and schedule changes affect residents throughout the region.

cards.headline: Florida homeowner finds seven-foot alligator in backyard pool
cards.teaser: A Florida resident discovered a large alligator had made itself at home in a swimming pool.
cards.body:
A Florida homeowner found a seven-foot alligator lounging in a backyard pool. The large reptile was discovered relaxing in the residential swimming pool.

The alligator measured seven feet in length when found in the pool. Florida residents occasionally encounter alligators on their properties during summer months.

cards.teaser: A judge approved the release of records related to Tiger Woods' DUI case.
cards.body:
A judge cleared records for release in the Tiger Woods DUI case. The judicial decision allows certain documents related to the case to become available.

The court ruling addresses records associated with Woods' DUI case. The judge's decision makes these records accessible.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman recognized for supporting little free libraries
hero.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman has been recognized for her work supporting little free libraries in the community.
hero.body:
A Fort Pierce woman has been recognized for her efforts supporting little free libraries throughout the area. The recognition highlights her contributions to the community literacy initiative.

Little free libraries are small book-sharing boxes that allow residents to take a book or leave a book for others in the neighborhood. The program promotes reading and community connection through these neighborhood sharing stations.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce estate into arts destination with global residency program
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination through its preservation of the historic Crain Estate and its internat.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and operating an international artist residency program. The nonprofit occupies the former home of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who traveled the world nine times collecting items for their Florida property. Jaxson Crain, a tile worker by trade, completed all the tiling throughout the facility from ground to walls to ceiling. The estate remains 90 percent unchanged from when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its stained glass and front patio bar. The Crains collected a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks in its design. Guided tours of the gardens and architecture are offered every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have inhabited the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing seven birds that have grown to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, believed to be 60 years old and the oldest peacock on the property, who walks with a limp and is hand-fed daily from his own bowls. The foundation's artist-in-residency program houses artists from around the world in simple but elegant accommodations. Art director Krystal Masters leads the art lab, offering classes for children and adults of all skill levels in mediums including sculpting and watercolor, with one-on-one classes designed for complete beginners.

cards.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: The wholesale retailer is planning to open its first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Costco is planning to open its first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie. The wholesale retailer's expansion to the area would mark its initial presence in the region.

The new location would bring the membership-based warehouse club to Treasure Coast shoppers for the first time. Port St. Lucie residents currently must travel outside the area to access Costco stores.

cards.teaser: Deputies report the body of a missing diver was found on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
The body of a missing diver was found on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet, according to deputies. The discovery followed a search for the missing diver in the area.

Fort Pierce Inlet is a popular location for diving and recreational boating activities. Deputies reported the recovery of the body from the coastal waters near the inlet.

hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic to Florida roads
hero.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home this Fourth of July weekend, marking an all-time high for the holiday.
hero.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with AAA estimating 72.2 million people will have journeyed at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that total, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day.

Friday's wet weather created difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd said the conditions were "really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the challenging weather, drivers continued their holiday trips. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Sebastian hosts watermelon eating contest on Independence Day
cards.teaser: Sebastian held a watermelon eating contest on July 4th as part of Independence Day celebrations.
cards.body:
Sebastian residents participated in a watermelon eating contest on Saturday, July 4, as part of the city's Fourth of July festivities. The event provided a way for residents to cool off during the holiday.

The contest took place on Independence Day in Sebastian. The watermelon eating competition was held during the holiday weekend celebrations in the city.

cards.headline: Vero Beach buries community time capsule to be opened in 2076
cards.body:
Vero Beach buried a community-wide time capsule on Friday that will remain sealed until 2076. The capsule contains items representing the city in 2026.

The burial took place on Friday, July 3. The time capsule will be opened 50 years from now, in 2076, allowing future generations to see what life was like in Vero Beach today.

The project represents a community effort to preserve the current era for residents who will live in Vero Beach five decades from now. The capsule will serve as a historical record of the city during this period.

The time capsule will remain buried in Vero Beach for the next half century. Residents in 2076 will be the first to open it and discover its contents.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition is becoming more expensive this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The price increases are driven by inflation across several key items. Ground beef prices rose 5.5%, buns increased 7.7%, and strawberries jumped 12.4% after being hit hard by a Florida frost. Ice cream prices also climbed 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have become more expensive. Potato prices dropped this year, benefiting shoppers looking for potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades offers the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends that families shop more strategically by comparing stores to find the best deals on their grocery lists. She also emphasized that cutting down food waste is important for families, and that begins with creating a meal plan.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools earning A or B grades.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year. The district achieved a record 93.5% graduation rate, and 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, received "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. District leaders reported that 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework, including Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the district's notable success stories is S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which improved from a "C" rating to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has led the school for 15 years, said staff modified the early childhood curriculum program three years ago, and those students are now in third grade performing at higher levels. The school also focused on challenging students and staff to raise expectations across campus. Three other schools also improved from "C" to "A" ratings this year: Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary. Superintendent Mike Burke said the "A" rating reflects the district's commitment to academic success and the hard work of students, teachers, school leaders, support staff, families, and community partners.

cards.headline: FSU Baseball lands commitment from FGCU pitcher Sebastian Lippman
cards.teaser: Florida State University's baseball program received a commitment from Florida Gulf Coast University right-handed pitcher Sebastian Lippman.
cards.body:
Florida State University's baseball team earned a commitment from FGCU right-handed pitcher Sebastian Lippman on Saturday. The Seminoles added the pitcher to their recruiting class.

Lippman pitched for Florida Gulf Coast University before committing to FSU. The addition strengthens the Seminoles' pitching roster for the upcoming season.
